tonight.headline: Rice and Barkley missed Thursday too; ESPN has zeroed both
body: Bad news first: Rashee Rice and Saquon Barkley both missed practice again on Thursday (NBC, 15 Oct), and ESPN now projects each at 0.0. This morning's two Sunday cards — Rice into the flex if active, Barkley for Tuten if cleared — are dead; Pickens and Tuten start outright. And Jacksonville's Week 7 bye takes Lawrence, your only quarterback, plus Tuten and Strange.

This week: 119.5 as set, which is the projection lineup, against Los Cachanillas' 95.4 — their quarterback slot holds Jalen Hurts, ruled out with a blood clot. ESPN 63%, up from 53% this morning. You swapped to the Patriots' defence and to Matt Gay at kicker before midday; Gay locks Sunday 14:25, and nothing on your roster plays tonight.

case.label: Why it moved
case.body: Hurts's ruling-out zeroes their quarterback slot unless they find another; Montgomery, also theirs, is out and did not travel to London (NBC, 15 Oct).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Los Cachanillas adding a quarterback before Sunday — likely, and it would claw back most of the gap. Rice or Barkley practising Friday would only restore bench depth: neither beats your starters unless ESPN reprices them.

whatWentWrong.title: Two seats changed hands this morning
whatWentWrong.lead: Defence: Jaguars to Ravens to Patriots in one minute (14:33-14:34 UTC). Kicker: Myers out, Matt Gay in (15:25 UTC).

case.label: This week
case.body: Both are coin-flip moves against the projection: the Patriots 7.4 sit 0.6 below the Ravens 8.0, who were added and dropped in the same minute; Gay 10.6 is exactly 2.0 above Myers 8.6. Neither costs priority — all free agents. Dropping the Jaguars removes one Jaguar from the Week 7 bye.

case.label: The churn rule
case.body: Both seats are now closed until 22 Oct. The defence seat has changed three times in two weeks; last week's stream already lost by 4 (closed WRONG).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers outscoring Gay tonight-plus-Sunday, or the Jaguars or Ravens defence outscoring the Patriots (archive, Week 6).
